transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I've been losing a lot of weight recently, and my family insisted I come in to get checked out. Honestly, I've just been eating very little lately, sometimes only a bite or two a day.
Are you intentionally avoiding food because you're afraid of gaining weight, or have you simply lost your appetite and interest in eating altogether?

I am intentionally skipping meals and eating as little as possible because I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight. It isn't that I've lost my appetite, but the thought of putting on any weight is just too scary for me to handle.
Do you ever experience episodes where you feel you lose control and eat a large amount of food, followed by trying to get rid of it by throwing up, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?
No, I never lose control or eat large amounts of food. I strictly control everything I eat, so I've never binged or forced myself to throw up. I just focus on avoiding food as much as possible.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ['Anorexia Nervosa', 'Bulimia Nervosa']. Based on the patient's explicit denial of binge eating and compensatory behaviors (such as purging or laxative use), and their description of strict food restriction leading to significant weight loss driven by an intense fear of gaining weight, Bulimia Nervosa can be ruled out. The presentation is highly consistent with Anorexia Nervosa, and we have sufficient evidence to make a final diagnosis.
